title: Security Review - Data Residency & Region Pinning

Devin to prepare region pinning configuration notes and KMS integration doc by 2025-06-25

summary: Redwood reviewed data residency and region-pinning capabilities for Finovate Bank. Customer confirmed EU residency requirement for EU customers and asked about cross-border processing, sub-processors, and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 and sub-processor list, produce region pinning config docs, and schedule KMS deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the account lead. Devin from our engineering team will cover the technical bits. Quick roll call?
[00:09] Laura (Finovate): Hi, Laura here, Head of Security.
[00:11] Tom (Finovate): Tom Reilly, Platform.
[00:13] Sven (Finovate): Sven from Legal, hello.
[00:16] Devin (Redwood SE): Hi all, Devin here.
[00:18] Maya: Great. Agenda is data residency and region pinning, sub-processor list, KMS/encryption questions, and audit logging. We have about 50 minutes. Is that good?
[00:27] Laura: Yep, perfect. High level: Finovate is doing a rollout in EU and US, and we need to ensure EU customer data stays in-region, no cross-border processing unless consented.
[00:38] Tom: We're particularly worried about third-party subprocessors and where inference happens. We currently host in eu-west-1 for EU users.
[00:46] Maya: Understood. Devin, do you want to start with region pinning capabilities?
[00:50] Devin: Sure. So Redwood supports region pinning at the request-routing layer. You can create route policies that say EU-only traffic pins to our EU capacity pools—we have dedicated hosted endpoints in eu-west-1 and also options for private deployments in customer VPCs.
[01:05] Tom: When you say pin, is that strict? i.e., no tokens or KV cache ever leave the EU?
[01:11] Devin: The default hosted path keeps model execution and KV cache in-region. For cross-border fallbacks there's a policy you can opt into but it's off by default. Note: some async analytics or aggregated telemetry might be processed in the control plane depending on config, but we can disable cross-border telemetry for EU accounts.
[01:28] Laura: Can you confirm audit logs and traces remain in-region as well? Our compliance team requires logs to be stored under EU controls.
[01:35] Devin: Yes, audit logs for API calls and per-request metadata can be configured to reside in the customer's region. We write logs to region-bound storage; we also support a push model to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets in the region.
[01:46] Sven: What about sub-processors? We need the list and specifics about any cross-border data sharing like for observability or backups.
[01:54] Maya: We'll send the current sub-processor list after the call. High level: compute and storage in EU are handled by our EU cloud region, backups are retained in-region unless you request geo-replication. Sub-processors that operate globally (e.g., CDN providers, monitoring) have contractual restrictions and we can redline DPAs.
[02:11] Laura: We also want to know about keys. Does Redwood manage encryption keys or can we bring our own key (BYOK)?
[02:17] Devin: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integration. For hosted we integrate with major cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). You can bring keys and we support envelope encryption so the ultimate key material is under your control. For private deployments you can use on-prem HSMs as well.
[02:33] Tom: Is there any metadata that might flow to Redwood control plane in US even with BYOK?
[02:39] Devin: Metadata like billing and org-level activity are in the control plane; however, request payloads, model inputs/outputs, and KV cache can be pinned. We can also mask or not store full request content in control plane if required. We'll share a diagram of what is considered "control plane" versus "data plane".
[02:56] Laura: What's your stance on lawful requests from foreign governments—like if US authorities request data stored in EU?
[03:03] Maya: We follow the legal process of the jurisdiction where data is stored. Our DPA outlines notice and challenge procedures; we'll provide that to legal. Sven, we'll loop you in.
[03:12] Sven: Good. Also we need the contractual language about sub-processor notifications and a 30-day cure window.
[03:18] Maya: Noted. We'll include standard sub-processor notification terms and can discuss specific redlines.
[03:23] [04:00] Devin: A few implementation details: region pinning happens at the route level—routes are assigned to geographic pools. We also provide a per-customer config flag to disable cross-region fallbacks; if disabled, requests queue or failover to on-prem/private. There's an option to replicate cached embeddings but only if you enable geo-replication.
[04:42] Tom: How do you handle model variants? If we use a large model hosted in US but a smaller quantized variant in EU, can the system automatically pick?
[04:51] Devin: Yes, smart routing can fallback to an EU-compatible variant. We maintain model catalogs with verified latency/perf profiles per region. But that does require you accept the variant policy; we'll note it in the SLA.
[05:05] Laura: For encryption at rest and in-transit, do you manage TLS certs? Are there mutual TLS options?
[05:12] Devin: We use TLS for all in-transit. We do offer mTLS for private deployments and mutual authentication for VPC peering. Certs are typically managed by us for hosted but you can bring certs in private.
[05:27] Sven: About logs: retention windows and ability to export for e-discovery?
[05:32] Maya: Logs retention is configurable. For enterprise plans we can set retention, export schedules, and even push weekly archives to your S3 in-region for e-discovery.
[05:44] Tom: Any sub-processors outside EU that touch EU customer data?
[05:48] Maya: For hosted EU region, the main compute and storage are in EU. Some monitoring and alerting services are multi-region—we can provide a version of our monitoring stack that's EU-only for customers with strict requirements.
[05:59] Laura: Can you provide the sub-processor list now?
[06:02] Maya: Not during the call, but we'll attach the most recent CSV in the follow-up email.
[06:07] Laura: Ok. For KMS: key rotation and key revocation—do you support customer-triggered key revocation and a KMS audit trail?
[06:15] Devin: Yes, if you bring your key, you control rotation and revocation in your KMS. We honor key revocation by losing the ability to decrypt the envelope—so backups become unreadable unless you export. We also produce KMS usage logs that you can ingest into your SIEM.
[06:30] Tom: About cross-border telemetry you mentioned—if we turn it off, does that impact performance/cost?
[06:36] Devin: There's a small operational cost: certain aggregated analytics won't be centralized which limits some platform-wide automated tuning. Latency for inference isn't affected if data plane is in-region. There's more manual tuning needed.
[06:49] Laura: Can you run a pilot where all EU traffic is pinned and telemetry off so we can validate?
[06:54] Maya: Absolutely. We can provision a pilot in EU region with telemetry disabled. That will be part of the next steps.
[06:59] [10:00] Devin: Quick note on subprocessors—we have a core list: cloud provider (AWS/Google/Azure in-region), logging provider (can be customer-hosted), metrics/observability (we can opt-in EU-only stack), CDN provider for edge routing, and some third-party security scanning. We'll provide exact names and contractual scoping.
[07:25] Tom: For the pilot, can the model weights be pinned to EU storage? We're trying to avoid model downloads from outside region.
[07:31] Devin: Yes, model artifacts can be hosted in EU object storage; our serving runtime pulls from region-local storage. For hosted we already have EU model cache.
[07:38] Laura: A nit: we need to know retention of KV cache and whether it counts as personal data.
[07:44] Devin: KV cache can be encrypted at rest and TTL'd. If you consider it personal data, you can configure immediate TTL or disable caching for sensitive routes.
[07:55] Sven: From legal side we want to confirm sub-processor notification period and data transfer clauses before contracting.
[07:59] Maya: We'll include standard 30-day notification and will work with you on DPA language.
[08:05] [12:00] Tom: On SSO: we use SAML with our IdP. Any special requirements?
[08:10] Maya: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, enforce RBAC via SCIM and fine-grained roles. For enterprise customers we can set up provisioning to limit access to only EU routes.
[08:22] Laura: Can we segregate developer access vs production access so devs can't see EU customer data?
[08:28] Devin: Yes, RBAC can restrict who can view logs or replay requests. We also support token scoping so API keys are scoped to route sets (EU-only) and can't be used elsewhere.
[08:39] Tom: Do we need to manage separate projects/environments for EU?
[08:42] Devin: You can either use route-level isolation or create separate orgs/accounts per region. Both are supported; separate orgs give stronger controls but more operational overhead.
[08:54] Laura: For compliance we'll likely want separate orgs for production EU workloads.
[08:58] Maya: Noted. We'll include recommendations in the follow-up doc.
[09:05] [20:00] Devin: A few more technicals: encryption in transit uses TLS1.2+ and perfect forward secrecy. At rest we support AES-256 with envelope encryption. Key access is logged via KMS. Our audit logs include request id, route, timestamp, actor, and bytes processed—content-level logging is optional and can be redacted.
[09:31] Laura: How long do you retain request-level logs by default?
[09:34] Devin: Default retention is 90 days on standard plan, configurable up to multiple years for enterprise. We can push to your archive bucket for long-term retention.
[09:44] Tom: If we request no content logs, will that break debug workflows?
[09:47] Devin: Debugging is harder: we'll rely on telemetry and metrics instead of full transcripts. We can also provide a time-limited enablement of content logging for specific debug windows under NDA.
[09:59] Laura: About model evals—are the eval datasets ever sent to third-party services?
[10:03] Devin: Not by default. Evaluations happening inside your account stay in-region. If you opt into external benchmarking or community models, those are opt-in.
[10:12] Sven: Are there EU-based sub-processors for support and escalation? We don't want US-based support staff to access data without controls.
[10:20] Maya: Support access is role-based and we can restrict remote access to EU data. For tiered escalation we have EU-based L2 support in working hours and can negotiate terms for on-call access.
[10:33] Tom: Regarding contract SLAs, we need latency SLOs per region and penalties if fallbacks route to other regions.
[10:40] Maya: SLA language can specify region-specific SLOs and exceptions for optional fallbacks. We'll include proposed wording.
[10:47] [30:00] Laura: Could you walk through an example request flow? From EU user to API to model execution and where logs land.
[10:52] Devin: Sure — EU user -> EU API Gateway -> Routed to EU serving pool -> model execution in EU compute -> outputs returned directly. Audit log written to EU log store and optionally pushed to customer S3 in eu-west-1. Control plane metadata (org config, billing) stays in control plane; we'll draw and send the diagram.
[11:16] Laura: If a user in EU triggers a function that calls an external tool hosted in US, how do you flag that?
[11:22] Devin: We instrument tool calls as part of the request trace and mark them; you can block or allow tool integrations per route.
[11:29] Tom: For the pilot, what's the fastest path? Hosted EU region with telemetry off and BYOK?
[11:34] Maya: Yes, we can provision a hosted EU pilot with BYOK and telemetry disabled. Expect a 2-week lead time for BYOK onboarding if you need key vetting.
[11:44] Laura: What about encryption key escrow—do you keep any copy?
[11:47] Devin: No, if BYOK is used we do not keep plaintext keys; we store only wrapped keys and cannot decrypt without the KMS.
[11:55] Sven: Contractually we need to ensure clear liability boundaries if keys are lost.
[11:59] Maya: We'll include standard KMS clauses and can discuss further with your legal.
[12:05] [40:00] Devin: One more technical ask—if you want zero cross-border telemetry, we'll need to configure both the ingestion endpoints and our alerting stack. It may disable some automated performance tuning, but we can run a manual review schedule.
[12:20] Tom: Fine. We accept manual tuning for now.
[12:23] Laura: For the pilot, please include a test plan and acceptance criteria: EU-only processing, BYOK, audit log push, and successful key rotation test.
[12:32] Maya: We'll draft that test plan and send as part of the follow-up.
[12:36] [50:00] Maya: Quick recap — action items and next steps: we'll send SOC2 and sub-processor list, Devin will produce config notes and KMS integration doc, and we schedule a KMS deep dive next week. Any other open items?
[12:52] Sven: Also send DPA draft and notification terms.
[12:55] Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[13:00] Tom: Thanks, bye.
[13:02] Laura: Thanks.
[13:04] Devin: Thanks all.
[13:06] [End of recording]
